title: Crops, Cropping Systems, Horticulture and Agroforestry
shortDescription: Seasons, cropping patterns, horticultural crops and tree-based systems.
genZNote: Kharif, Rabi, Zaid — farming's three seasons and a lot of easy pickups. Add trees on farms and you've got agroforestry.

sections.heading: Crops and Seasons
sections.body: Crop groups: cereals, millets, pulses, oilseeds, fibre, sugar, fodder, plantation, spices, horticultural. Gujarat leads in groundnut, cotton, castor, cumin, isabgol among others (check yearly figures).

table.caption: Cropping seasons
rows: Rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soybean, tur
Wheat, barley, gram, mustard, pea, linseed

sections.heading: Cropping Systems
bullets: Monocropping, multiple cropping, double cropping, sequential cropping, relay cropping, intercropping (mixed vs row), crop rotation (e.g. cereal–legume), ratoon cropping.
Benefits: soil fertility (legumes fix nitrogen), pest breaks, risk spreading; indices: cropping intensity and land-equivalent ratio.

sections.heading: Horticultural Crops and Agroforestry
bullets: Horticulture: fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops, medicinal plants; high value per unit area; India is among the top fruit and vegetable producers.
Post-harvest handling: harvesting maturity, grading, pre-cooling, packing, cold chain.

Agroforestry: trees with crops/livestock — agri-silviculture, silvopasture, agri-horticulture, boundary plantation, windbreaks/shelterbelts, home-gardens; India's National Agroforestry Policy (2014) was the first of its kind in the world.
Benefits: carbon sequestration, fodder, fuelwood, shade and income diversification.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Crops are grown in seasonal and intensive systems; horticulture and agroforestry diversify farm income and ecological services.
keyFacts: Kharif June–Oct; Rabi Oct–Mar; Zaid Mar–Jun.

highYieldFacts: Rice and cotton are kharif; wheat and gram are rabi.
commonTraps: Do not mix intercropping with mixed cropping.
